title: tf: add drift-resistant gpu_nodepool module with overlay tfstate and IAM templating
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: Private installs running GPU workloads have produced recurring terraform drift between per-tenant GPU nodepool resources and the central tfstate when clusters are upgraded or when operator-managed labels change. This PR introduces a new gpu_nodepool module built for drift resilience and a lightweight tfstate overlay pattern to isolate tenant-scoped transient resources during rolling upgrades.

What this does (single-line summary): Adds a drift-resistant modules/gpu_nodepool with guarded lifecycle rules, introduces modules/tfstate_overlay for non-destructive overlay state attachments, and templates IAM role bindings to reduce manual reconciliation.

Key changes and rationale:
- New module modules/gpu_nodepool: encapsulates nodepool creation, taint/label reconciliation, and a controlled replacement flow (pre-drain hook + nodegroup swap). Uses lifecycle.prevent_destroy guards on cloud resources that are sensitive to accidental deletes and exposes a replace_strategy variable to opt into safe replace behavior during major upgrades.
- New module modules/tfstate_overlay: implements an optional overlay state mechanism (concatenate state views) so tenant-scoped transient resources (e.g., ephemeral GPU leases, per-tenant NAT allocations) can be kept in an overlay state rather than the canonical cluster tfstate. This limits lock contention and reduces blast radius when rolling back or migrating.
- IAM templating in modules/iam/role_templates.tf: converts several hand-maintained role bindings into parameterized templates to ensure stable role identity between installs and to make drift detection faithful (role ARNs are stable across migration).
- scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh: a migration helper that creates a reversible snapshot and performs a non-blocking copy of selected resources to an overlay state backend. Includes dry-run and rollback modes.
- docs/examples/private/overlay-migration.md: documents step-by-step migration and rollback for on-prem customers with constrained maintenance windows.

Backward compatibility and safety: All changes opt-in by default. The new overlay is disabled unless tfstate_overlay.enabled = true in the root module. Lifecycle.prevent_destroy guards can be relaxed with a flag for operators that prefer destructive redeploys. The migration script is provided for manual, audited migrations.

Testing done: unit Terraform plan tests (mock backends), end-to-end on a staging cluster with a simulated tenant eviction and rollback, and k8s node drain simulation for replacement flow. Linter/format fixed on second commit.

Checklist:
- [x] Module implementation
- [x] Unit plan tests
- [x] e2e staging validation
- [x] Documentation and migration guide
- [x] CI green after lint fix

Related: ENG-10123 (tenant rollout reliability), ENG-10345 (tfstate scale improvements).

review_comments: Diego: Can we avoid lifecycle.prevent_destroy on the autoscaler role? That broke a previous restore in INT-742. Suggested making it opt-in via variable.

Lila: Please add explicit plan diffs in the docs for the overlay switch — operators need to know what to expect during cutover.
Priya: Added examples/overlay-migration.md with concise plan diffs and rollback commands.
Owen: CI failed on tfsec in the first run (hard-coded ARN). After templating roles, tfsec warnings resolved.
Priya: Verified tfsec and added an explicit test in tests/terraform/plans to assert no hard-coded ARNs remain.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after two approval reviews and CI green. Migration docs and scripts included in the squash commit. Author validated rollback path on staging.
release_notes: Introduces a new gpu_nodepool TF module with guarded lifecycle and an optional tfstate overlay mechanism for tenant-scoped transient resources. Includes IAM role templating and a reversible tfstate migration helper. Opt-in via tfstate_overlay.enabled=false by default.
